summary: The team is executing a China-first global marketing strategy, with Asia Star and Intelligent China as top priorities, while finalizing the Knowledge website redesign and managing urgent IT and event logistics.
summaryDetail: The most critical initiative right now is the China-focused global marketing push, with Asia Star and the new Intelligent China program prioritized for SEO/AI-search visibility; the Intelligent China webpage must launch and drive traffic, and Joseph is drafting target prompts and building customer profiles from Asia Star participants and CRM leads. The Knowledge website redesign is nearing completion, with decisions to keep the two-menu structure, adopt a card-based UX, and integrate BCI/BSI indices, but pre-launch fixes and a working session to mark design feedback are still pending. This week, the team must resolve an Outlook account lockout by updating stale credentials across devices and confirming backend unlock with JSB, and complete the Google Ads conversion tracking audit. Upcoming priorities include preparing for the Women in Leadership Forum in November, finalizing the English obituary for Professor Jon Liao, and updating school women's figures for the emcee script.

decisions.text: Use the new password across all devices and update any stale saved credentials.
Remove the dedicated videos section; videos will be dispersed by topic across the site instead of having their own category.
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge menu and School menu) as a good approach.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the very top of the homepage.
Bring the BCI (and BSI) index banner into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage.
Adopt the card-based UX design that helps readers distinguish content types (professor analysis, etc.).
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as top two programs; US partner programs (Stanford, Columbia) on hold initially.
Berkeley program suggested as a possible third priority, to be considered in the audit phase.
No need to involve legal in the PRME data security incident at this point, as no real damage has occurred
